chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the times for the Witr prayer, and he said: 'The one I prefer is the first dawn.' And I asked him about the best time of the night, and he said: 'The remaining third.' And I asked him about Witr after the dawn of morning, and he said: 'Yes, my father would sometimes perform Witr after the dawn had broken.'
ai.seo_question: What is the best time to perform the Witr prayer according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s preference for the first dawn (Al-Fajr Al-Awwal) for Witr, while also validating the permissibility of delaying it until after the true dawn breaks, a practice attributed to the Prophet. It underscores the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of this voluntary night prayer, balancing spiritual preference with practical allowance. The emphasis on the 'remaining third' of the night for general night prayers further connects to the Quranic description of the righteous who pray during the night.
